terms.grammar: adjective; with cum or the dative
evidence: Cic. Phil. 9.15: mors ejus vītae sānctissimē āctae
terms.comment: Cicero’s word above all (Lewis & Short); it also means fitting, proper.

terms.grammar: adjective, third declension; with cum or the dative
evidence: Cic. Brut. 117: vīta cum disciplīnā (Lewis & Short, s.v. congruō)
Cic. Leg. 1.30: ōrātiō verbīs discrepāns, sententiīs congruēns

terms.comment: Hoc nōn convenit cum eō quod dīxistī: “this isn’t consistent with what you said”.

phrases.latin: quod quidem erat cōnsentāneum cum iīs litterīs, quās ego Rōmae accēperam
phrases.english: which was indeed consistent with the letter I had received at Rome
a speech differing in its words but consistent in its thoughts

phrases.latin: Hoc nōn convenit cum eō quod heri dīxistī.
phrases.english: This isn’t consistent with what you said yesterday.

sources: Lewis & Short: consentaneus · Lewis & Short: congruo · Lewis & Short: convenio
